source.title: LLM Gesticulator: Leveraging Large Language Models for Scalable and Controllable Co-Speech Gesture Synthesis
source.authors: Haozhou Pang; Tianwei Ding; Lanshan He; Ming Tao; Lu Zhang; Qi Gan

record.file_problem: not stated; the full paper text is present, but Figure 7's plotted values are not included in the supplied text
record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly validates a scaling effect by measuring gesture-generation quality across QWen model sizes, using FGD rather than held-out language-model loss.
record.gate_note: The scaling experiment reports FGD for gesture generation across model sizes. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy, fit or test power laws for parameters/tokens/compute, compare extrapolated predictions, or test compute-optimal allocations. Figure 7's plotted values and separate series cannot be read from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The paper fine-tunes QWen1.5 models at 0.5B, 1.8B, 4B and 7B on co-speech gesture generation and reports FGD by model size (Sec. 4.5, Fig. 7). This is a downstream result on scale in a new setting, so it bears on V6. It is T3, not T2: it applies scale to a new task and does not use a different method aimed at the original loss question. There is no loss measure, no power-law fit and no compute or token axis, so the other versions are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report performance gains as model size increases and call this consistent with the scaling law, demonstrating their framework's scalability.
record.recipe_differences: This is a gesture-generation quality sweep using FGD across model sizes, not a held-out cross-entropy power-law fit or compute-optimal allocation study.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper describes multiple training configurations, but the supplied text does not expose their separate Figure 7 outcomes.
record.problems: The scaling evidence is reported for gesture-generation quality rather than held-out language-model loss. Figure 7's values are unavailable in the supplied text, and separate results for the mentioned training configurations cannot be assessed.
record.rows_left_out: No other scaling results are reported in extractable form in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss vs parameters, tokens or compute; no loss is reported.
No fits on small runs and no extrapolation to larger runs.
No shape or architecture sweep at fixed parameter count.
Fine-tuning on a motion/audio token modality is a candidate setting, but no power-law form is fitted or shown.
No prediction from pretraining loss, no quantitative scaling relation, and no check across the other metrics (BeatAlign, Diversity) by size.
No examination of fitting choices or curvature.

missing.what: Numeric FGD values per model size and per training configuration (fine-tune only vs pretrain then fine-tune)

record.verdict_notes: The term 'scaling law' is used loosely here, to mean monotone improvement with backbone size; no power law is fitted. Table 1 compares 7B with and without pretraining and other methods; it is not a scale result. The FGD column in Table 1 has only four values for five rows, so the alignment of values to rows is unclear.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation trends.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
The study reports gesture-generation quality across model sizes, but does not test predictions from pretraining loss or fit a quantitative downstream scaling relationship.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocations on setup and fitting choices, and departures from a single power law.

rows.subject: QWen1.5 series (0.5B, 1.8B, 4B, and 7B)
rows.stage_stated: fine-tuned; some configurations involve pretraining followed by fine-tuning
rows.operation_detail: Compared gesture-generation quality across QWen1.5 model sizes.

conditions.value: The text mentions configurations using speakers 2, 4, 6, and 8, and configurations with pretraining followed by fine-tuning; separate plotted results are unavailable.

rows.note: The authors state that larger models produce higher-quality action sequences and describe Figure 7 as showing the impact of model size on FGD. The plotted numbers and configuration-specific results are not present in the supplied text.
rows.check: Values are figure-only and cannot be read from the text. The state rests on the authors' words: larger models produce higher quality action sequences. Only four sizes are compared. No functional form is fitted and no uncertainty is given, so 'predictably' is not quantified. Results for the two configurations (fine-tune only vs pretrain then fine-tune) cannot be separated. The tranche should be T3, not T2.
